entries.place: The Redmist estate, at the gate
entries.what_happened: Julian told the maid and gatekeeper he was going to Marchand Street, east side, and asked them to say plainly if any of the staff would send word to friends there. The maid admitted half the staff is from around there and that by tonight they would know he went to Marchand and want to know why; the gatekeeper said Marguerite had already said plenty in the staff's hearing. Julian told them not to lie but to tell it straight: their master went to call on a widow of the family name and would say more when done, and asked the telling wait until the carriage was out of sight. The gatekeeper opened the gate. Carla told Julian the gatekeeper had a cousin on the east side and that it is a small city.

entries.place: The carriage, on the streets toward Marchand Street
entries.what_happened: In the carriage Julian said that if the gatekeeper's cousin had already heard something before they knocked, he would know how fast word travels in Islaport. He asked whether they should stop at Marchand Mutual first or leave the bank to Jezebel. Carla said Jezebel has the bank and they should keep their hands clean until she rings, because two strangers asking after a widow's account would make a story by afternoon; Jezebel could ask as the estate's accountant. She said the turn onto Marchand was the last stretch. Julian told the driver to stop short of the house rather than at it, and said he would mind the gap when they knocked.

entries.place: The Hollis house on Marchand Street
entries.what_happened: The carriage stopped short of the house. Carla stayed at the gate while Julian went to the door. Tomas Hollis answered, trowel in hand, and said whatever Julian was selling they had enough of it. Julian gave his name as Julian Redmist and said Bernard had left him a key with Marguerite's name on it; he came to learn what it opens and what the name meant to Bernard. Tomas let him in, said Hollis was his father's family and his mother kept the name, and told him to wipe his feet. Julian said he would say his piece plainly and that if she refused him the key stayed with him either way. Tomas went to the parlor and returned to show him in. Marguerite, shawled by the window, said she had begun to think the will a rumor the city made up to pass the winter.

entries.place: The parlor of the Hollis house
entries.what_happened: Julian told Marguerite the will was real, cited twelve years of quarterly payments with the last noted 'for the boy's schooling' in Bernard's own hand, and set the key on the table, tag up. Marguerite said the key was to Edmund's strongbox, which the bank would not open to her without a court; Bernard had promised to sort it before he grew too sick to leave the house, and she had let the silence speak for both of them. She said the box belongs to Tomas. Julian said Tomas should turn the key and asked which bank held it. Marguerite said Marchand Mutual held Edmund's accounts and the strongbox went to the Islaport Trust when the old branch closed; a deputy manager and a rulebook would want a court order unless the paper named Julian. Tomas asked whether Bernard had put Julian's or his own name on the box. Julian said he did not know, that the will named him the fortune but no strongbox and no Tomas. He proposed going to the Trust the next day with Tomas, paying for a lawyer if paper was needed, and said Tomas could keep the key and go alone if he preferred. Tomas said mornings were no good and set the meeting at the Trust at one o'clock, with the key and the will's paper. On the step he said his mother would spend the night arguing him out of going, not from being against Julian but from being against hoping.

entries.place: The carriage returning to the Redmist estate, and the estate gate
entries.what_happened: Julian told Tomas that if his mother talked him round by one o'clock he should send word to the estate and Julian would not hold it against him. Outside the gate Julian's shoulders dropped. In the carriage Carla said the street was quiet and the gatekeeper's cousin had not beaten them there, and asked about the boy. Julian said Tomas was steady and had taken the key because his mother left the decision to him, but had no experience with men like deputy managers and might not know whether to bow or stand his ground; Julian said he would watch the deputy more than the box and make sure nobody talked Tomas out of holding the key. Carla said they needed a lawyer who knew the Trust's rulebook and that Jezebel would know who. At the estate the gatekeeper met the carriage with a folded note from Jezebel, to be given the moment Julian was back, and said the staff had been told about Marchand straight, as Julian asked.
